title: Scalar mate compatibility with strict compactification refinements
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum of [def-pur-conventions], with algebraic closure $k$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and finite extensions $E\subset F$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Write $A=\mathcal O_E$, $B=\mathcal O_F$, $t=\varpi_E$, $v=\varpi_F$ and $e\geq1$ with $tB=v^eB$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type between separated finite-type $k$-schemes, and fix a compactification $c=(X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p_c}Y)$ with $j$ open and $p_c$ proper [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. On the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], put $R_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$, $S_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,W}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and $C_W=-\otimes^L_{R_W}S_W$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Let $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\mathcal O_E)$, the derived-complete bounded constructible category with a uniform Tor-amplitude interval for all reductions [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Write $A_n=A/t^n$, $B_n=B/t^nB=B/v^{en}$, $M_n=M\otimes^L_{R_X}(A_n)_X$, and $C_W^{(n)}=-\otimes^L_{(A_n)_W}(B_n)_W$. For $H=E,F$, let $P_H^c$ be the integral compact-support functor attached to $c$, defined as the total derived inverse limit of its finite separately derived proper/open images [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support].

Use the strict reduction lifts $\mathcal T_E^c(M)$ and $\mathcal T_F^c(C_XM)$ of [lem-weil-compact-support-reduction-tower-functor], restricted to the discrete constant ring sheaves $\underline A$ and $\underline B$. A strict tower means a complex in $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{Mod}(\underline A_W))$ or its $B$ analogue, with its ordinary derived category [def-weil-inverse-system, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. A superscript $(e)$ retains indices $en$ with composite transitions. Put $T=-\otimes_A B$ on constant-coefficient tower complexes; all finite coefficient objects are regarded as constant integral modules by restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars].

For a second compactification $d$ of $f$ and a refinement $r:c\to d$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], let $\rho_H(r):\mathcal T_H^c\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal T_H^d$ be the normalized strict proper/open comparison of [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus], for $H=E,F$, taken in the displayed direction by inversion when necessary. Use the scalar mate $q_\bullet$ of [lem-pur-compact-support-strict-scalar-mate]. Then
$$(\rho_F(r)_{C_XM})^{(e)}\circ q_\bullet^c
=q_\bullet^d\circ T(\rho_E(r)_M)$$
as morphisms in the derived category of strict $B$-towers, before evaluation or inverse limit.

The equality uses the actual refinement normalization: in the proper/open pullback factorization the open map is the projection onto the clopen refinement section, identity on that section and zero on its complementary open component, and the proper comparison is its adjunction mate. Constant finite-free tensor carries this projection to the same projection and preserves its ordered proper/open mate. The finite evaluations have bounded-below finite-coefficient etale-origin witnesses; no uniform lower bound is required. The square respects identity refinements, composable refinements, proper/open composition normalizations and common refinements. Thus its total-limit square, using the augmentation-preserving Roos comparisons and the constant/completed equivalence, is the square for the canonical compactification comparisons of the integral compact-support definition [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support].

proof.text: The open immersions in a compactification are quasi-compact: apply [lemma-nagata-open-immersion-qc-over-separated-target] to $X\xrightarrow{j_c}\overline X_c\to Y$. Its composite is the finite-type, hence quasi-compact, map $f$; the second map is proper, hence separated and quasi-separated by [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated]. The same applies to $d$. For any of the proper/open squares used below, write its top, bottom, left and right maps as $k:V\hookrightarrow W$, $i:S\hookrightarrow Z$, $r:V\to S$, $p:W\to Z$. Use exactly the $\beta$, the clopen lift $s:V\hookrightarrow W\times_ZS$, the projection $\pi_s$, and $\alpha_H=\beta_H$ followed by the open pushforward of $\pi_s$ and open composition, from [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus]. Its proper mate is $\gamma_H:i_{!,H}R_{r,H}\to R_{p,H}k_{!,H}$. In a refinement $V=S=X$, $r=1_X$, $k=j_c$, $i=j_d$ and $p=u:\overline X_c\to\overline X_d$. The first step verifies precisely the calculus's finite-evaluation hypotheses, so its comparison on these input towers is invertible.

proof.text: For each scheme $W$ write $T_W=-\otimes_A B$. On ordinary strict tower complexes it is exact: the basis from [lem-pur-compact-support-coefficient-models] identifies its underlying $A$-module functor with a finite direct sum, and exactness of towers is levelwise by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. Thus its descent to the derived category is represented by this same functor. Put $h_u:G_{u,B}T\xrightarrow{\sim}TG_{u,A}$ for the constant-coefficient pullback/tensor identification, and $b_j:Tj_{!,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{!,B}T$. Use the diagram-site open maps of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. The map $b_j$ sends a local open summand $x\otimes b$ to the same tensor in that summand. The maps $h_u$ commute with pullback composition: both composites pull back $x$ and leave $b$ unchanged. All these are maps of $B$-module complexes and commute with the tower transitions. Denote by $a_u:TR_{u,A}\to R_{u,B}T$ the proper adjunction mate of $h_u$, as normalized in [lem-pur-compact-support-strict-scalar-mate].

proof.text: Prove compatibility with beta inverse by its specified open-unit transpose. The normalized scalar/pullback comparisons commute with gComp by [lem-pur-strict-scalar-pull-composition]; invert and paste the two compositor equations, retaining the equality transport of the commutative scheme square, to obtain the scalar square for squareG inverse. By [lem-pur-strict-scalar-open-unit], scalar extension preserves both open units. The open scalar map is invertible by [lem-pur-compact-support-strict-scalar-mate]. Transport the source through it and apply the open adjunction Hom equivalence. Naturality moves the source and target scalar/pullback comparisons through the unit formulas. Substitute the squareG square and the two defining beta-inverse transpose equations. Both transposes become the target open unit followed by its squareG inverse. Injectivity of the Hom equivalence proves the beta-inverse square. For a cartesian square, cancel the invertible beta maps to obtain scalar_beta. This argument applies to the whole derived strict tower category and does not use evaluation faithfulness.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-strict-scalar-open-unit] to the A-tower pulled back along the clopen immersion. The pi_components theorem identifies pullback of each intrinsic projector with the corresponding open unit. Naturality of strictScalarPull rewrites pullback of the proposed scalar square; the open-unit equation and naturality of the B-unit identify its sides. Compose with the invertible clopen openToR comparison and apply the geometric adjunction Hom bijection to recover equality of the original strict derived B-tower maps. This proves scalar_clopen_projection, including zero on the complementary component. Now expand alpha into beta for the canonical fibre-product square, its squareLift clopen projector, and the specified open and inverse-image compositors. Paste scalar_beta from Step 4, scalar_clopen_projection, [lem-pur-strict-scalar-open-composition], and the inverse form of [lem-pur-strict-scalar-pull-composition]. Naturality moves the scalar/open maps across the projector and the endpoint compositors; the adjacent scalar/pullback factors combine to the named inverse-image compositor equation. Equality transport along squareLift followed by the two projections is retained on both sides. The proved categorical alpha_pasting equation assembles these factors into exactly scalar_properOpen_alpha for every commutative proper/open square, including noncartesian squares.

proof.text:
Take proper-adjunction mates of the cube in Step 5, using [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] (1)-(2), first along the coefficient/pullback faces and then along $G_p\dashv R_p$ and $G_r\dashv R_r$. The mates of $h_p,h_r$ are $a_p,a_r$; the mates of $\alpha_A,\alpha_B$ are the specified $\gamma_A,\gamma_B$ of [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus]. Thus the two pasted mates are
$$R_{p,B}(b_k)\,(a_pk_{!,A})\,(T\gamma_A)
=(\gamma_BT)\,(i_{!,B}a_r)\,(b_iR_{r,A}).$$
Their common source is $T_Zi_{!,A}R_{r,A}$ and target is $R_{p,B}k_{!,B}T_V$. For normalization, $a_{u,N}$ is the transpose of $T\varepsilon_{u,A,N}\circ h_{u,R_{u,A}N}$, while $\gamma_H$ is $R_{p,H}k_{!,H}\varepsilon_{r,H}\circ R_{p,H}(\alpha_HR_{r,H})\circ\eta_{p,H}i_{!,H}R_{r,H}$. These are precisely the ordered maps in [lem-pur-compact-support-strict-scalar-mate] and the strict calculus. Mate pasting uses the composite adjunctions with their specified unit and counit, so this establishes the equation in $D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(\underline B)))$ itself.

proof.text:
The displayed direction in the question is $\rho_H(u)=\Theta_H(u)^{-1}$. The isomorphism assertion and this direction are also recorded by [lem-cbc-complete-proetale-refinement-exchange-coherence]. Precompose Step 7 by $T\Theta_E(u)^{-1}$ and postcompose by $(\Theta_F(u)^{(e)})^{-1}$. This gives exactly
$$(\rho_F(u)_{C_XM})^{(e)}\circ q_\bullet^c=q_\bullet^d\circ T(\rho_E(u)_M).$$
This inversion is performed within the derived $B$-tower category, so it preserves the established normalization and does not require evaluation functors to be faithful.

proof.text: For identities and composites use $C_{\mathrm{id}}=1$ and $C_{v\circ u}=C_uC_v$ from [lem-cbc-complete-proetale-refinement-exchange-coherence], with $C_u=\Theta_H(u)$. Pasting the two scalar squares in Step 8 cancels the middle $q$ and gives the square for the composite; identity refinements give the identity square. For compatible proper/open composition towers, Step 6 applies to each commutative proper/open square, including a noncartesian one. The vertical and horizontal composition equations and the pasted-$\alpha$ normalization of [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus], together with proper-composition mate pasting, identify their pasted scalar square with that for the prescribed composite. Common refinements exist by [prop-compactification-refinement]. The common-refinement comparisons are $I_{12}=C_{u_2}^{-1}C_{u_1}$ by the first cited node, independent of the choices and satisfying the cocycle equation. Apply Step 8 to both arrows and invert/paste to obtain the corresponding square for $I_{12}$. This proves all the identity, composition and common-refinement assertions before taking limits. The proper/open composition assertion is now proved by scalar_composition_pasting applied to scalar_properOpen_gamma, strictScalarOpenComposition and strictScalarProperComposition. The first helper moves the central mate across scalar extension, the second handles the open compositor (including equality transport), and the third handles the proper compositor (including equality transport). Naturality pastes the three exact equations to give compositionD compatibility.

proof.text:
Countable products of these constant-ring pro-etale module sheaves are exact by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. Use the total-limit Roos realization of [lem-sf-strict-roos-derived-limit-comparison] and the specified scalar/product map $\tau$ and cofinal block map $r_e$ of [lem-pur-compact-support-roos-cofinality]. Their naturality turns Step 8 into the limit square for
$$c^c=r_{e,c}^{-1}\,R\!\lim(q_\bullet^c)\,\tau_c.$$
Explicitly, naturality gives $R\!\lim(T\rho_E)\tau_c=\tau_dT(R\!\lim\rho_E)$ and $R\!\lim(\rho_F^{(e)})r_{e,c}=r_{e,d}R\!\lim\rho_F$; substitute these in $R\!\lim$ of Step 8 and cancel the invertible $r_e$. The resulting equality is $(R\!\lim\rho_F)c^c=c^d\,T(R\!\lim\rho_E)$. The same cited cofinality lemma says that $\tau,r_e$ preserve the augmentations, so this calculation uses the prescribed normalized total-limit comparisons. It preserves the identity, composition and common-refinement equations since every map used is natural.

proof.text: Finally transport this whole limit square through [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] and the ordinary/strict scalar identification of [lem-pur-compact-support-coefficient-models]. Their stated identifications carry quotient transitions and total derived limits, together with completion units, to their completed-coefficient counterparts. The object at a vertex is therefore the reduction-limit compact-support value of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. At finite level the strict comparison evaluates to the normalized proper/open comparison, by [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus]; its inverse followed by the proper compositor is exactly the comparison specified in [def-sf-refinement-comparison-isomorphism]. The integral comparison in the reduction-limit construction is the total limit of these specified strict maps, so transporting the already proved strict/limit square gives the asserted square for the canonical integral compactification comparisons. This identification uses the actual total-limit construction and its units, rather than inferring equality of integral maps from equal finite reductions.
